artifacts.summary: Execution summary for all 6 phases fixing the six catalogued Typst layout defects, with per-defect before/after evidence and documented deviations.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed all six catalogued display/layout defects in typst/FormalFoundations.typ and typst/BimodalReference.typ (overflowing display equations, an unbreakable dotted Lean identifier fixed systemically at its template.typ source, a table-column overlap, an unbreakable module-map identifier, and a 24-row table overflowing its page) using a Playwright screenshot loop plus a PyMuPDF bounding-box scanner for mechanical verification. Both documents compile cleanly with unchanged page counts, typst-sync-check.sh passes, and zero mathematical content changed anywhere.

memory_candidates.content: Typst auto-column-sizing interacts badly with mixed breakable/unbreakable cells in the same table column: giving a sym.zws break opportunity to only some cells in a column can shrink that column's computed width below what the still-unbreakable cells need, causing them to overflow into the next column. Fix: apply the break opportunity uniformly to every cell in the column, and consider explicit columns: (auto, 1fr, auto) width behavior if the longest breakable label still collides at auto-computed width.

In Typst, `#{ show figure: set block(breakable: true); figure(...) }` scopes a breakable-figure show-rule to exactly one #figure call (block-local, via a code block), letting one specific table span page boundaries with header/caption repeated correctly while every other figure in the document remains atomic. This is the correct idiom for making a single oversized table/figure breakable without a document-wide show rule.

A PyMuPDF bounding-box overflow scanner comparing text/drawing bboxes against a document's declared text-block geometry is an effective mechanical backstop for Typst layout defects, but must explicitly exclude the auto-numbering page-footer (Typst places page numbers in the margin band by design under #set page(numbering: ...), which otherwise shows up as a 100%-of-pages false positive.

reflection.what_worked: Validating every fix idiom (row breaks, sym.zws break opportunities, the breakable show-rule scope, column width behavior) in an isolated scratch compile before touching the real files caught two non-obvious Typst behaviors early (auto-column-sizing desync with mixed breakable cells; the page-footer false positive) without wasting real-file edit cycles.
reflection.what_was_hard: Diagnosing why applying a break opportunity to only the two originally-named long identifiers in the DerivationTree table broke unrelated, previously-fine rows required a dedicated isolated probe to root-cause a subtle Typst auto-width computation interaction, not something visible from reading the source alone.
reflection.what_was_missed: The plan's Phase 4 Scope Hypothesis predicted a page-count increase from making Table 8 breakable; the actual result was no page-count change at all, corrected during implementation rather than anticipated.
reflection.successes: All six catalogued defects resolved with zero mathematical content changes anywhere (verified by source diff at every phase), both documents compile cleanly with unchanged page counts, and the one small side-effect discovered (an 8.1pt caption-line technicality) was investigated to a documented, evidenced conclusion rather than glossed over.
